newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: BOE's George urges Maastricht criteria adherence.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George urges Maastricht criteria adherence.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George on Tuesday urged the European Union to adhere to Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria to avoid potential problems.

"There is a risk that the single monetary policy - the single interest rate - which is a necessary corollary of a single currency may not in the event prove to be appropriate to the domestic needs," George told the two-day Gulf Economic Forum which opened in Bahrain on Tuesday.
"This risk was quite clearly recognised by the drafters of the Maastricht Treaty," he said.
He said EU countries would have no possibility of adjusting interest rates or their exchange rate independently, and they would have only limited scope for independent fiscal adjustment.

"Without much greater structural, supply-side, flexibility than is evident at present in some continental European countries, the result could be...protracted economic weakness and persistent high unemployment in some countries, if the European Central Bank pursued a firm monetary policy," he said.
Or the outcome would be "unwanted inflation in the economically stronger countries, if the ECB were more accommodating," he added.
"This is why meeting the convergence criteria, in economic substance not simply in a formal sense, is so important," he said.
George also said a single currency was not a necessary complement to the single market.
But he said the unique inter-European exchange rate that would be provided by a single currency could greatly enhance the benefits derived from the single market.
"It would...no doubt be a desirable complement to the single market," he added.
